w: William Henry Playfair's neo-classical pile at the junction of the Mound and Princes Street, built 1822-6 for the Royal Scottish Academy. Alongside its neighbour, the National Gallery, its columned facade helped earn Edinburgh the nickname 'the Athens of the North.' Now Category A listed, still its original job.
s: Playfair's pile behind Edinburgh's 'Athens of the North' tag
_facts: Built by William Henry Playfair in 1822-6 at the junction of the Mound and Princes Street
Neo-classical design, alongside the National Gallery of Scotland, helped earn Edinburgh the nickname 'the Athens of the North'
Today a Category A listed building

w: Officially the King Fahd Mosque, tucked on Potterrow among university buildings. Architect Basil Al Bayati took over six years and £3.5M to fuse Islamic form with Modernist Scots baronial style -- chandeliers, a vast carpet, almost no furniture, women praying from a balcony above a hall built for a thousand.
s: Islamic tradition meets Scots baronial style on Potterrow
_facts: Officially the King Fahd Mosque and Islamic Centre of Edinburgh, on Potterrow
Designed by Dr Basil Al Bayati, took more than six years to complete at a cost of £3.5M
Combines traditional Islamic features with a Modernist Scots baronial style
Main hall holds over 1,000 worshippers, with women praying from a balcony above

w: Thirty-five acres, the last scrap of the old Burgh Muir, a woodland once stretching south to the Jordan Burn. James IV ordered it cleared in 1508, and the timber went into the Old Town, framing houses and forestairs of the Lawnmarket and West Bow. Unlike the Meadows next door, this ground was never a loch: always dry.
s: The last scrap of Burgh Muir, cleared by royal decree in 1508
_facts: 35 acres of open parkland in Bruntsfield, the last vestige of the ancient Burgh Muir woodland
Unlike the adjoining Meadows, which formerly held a loch, Bruntsfield Links has always been dry ground
The woodland was cleared by decree of James IV in 1508
Much of the felled timber built the timber-fronted houses and forestairs of the Lawnmarket and West Bow

w: When the Union Canal's eastern basins were filled in and the canal truncated in 1921, Lochrin Basin became its new terminus -- and the Leamington Lift Bridge was hauled here from its old Fountainbridge crossing. The basin is now the centrepiece of Edinburgh Quay, winner of Best Regeneration at the 2005 Design Awards.
s: Where the Union Canal quietly ran out of road in 1921
_facts: When the Union Canal's eastern basins were filled in and truncated in 1921, Lochrin Basin became the new eastern terminus
The Leamington Lift Bridge was moved here from its former Fountainbridge crossing
Lochrin Basin is the centrepiece of the Edinburgh Quay development, voted Best Regeneration project in Scotland at the 2005 Scottish Design Awards
It is also the eastern end of the Forth and Clyde Canal Pathway
